sampling_model.design: Conditional on each fixed covariate stratum, \(Z\) is randomized with known \(\pi_z(x)=P(Z=z\mid X=x)\) and \(\min_{x,z}\{P(X=x),\pi_z(x)\}\ge\pi_*\); the observed count vector satisfies \(N_n\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\{n,p_n(u)\}\).
sampling_model.units: The categorical support \(\mathcal J\), rational wage grid \(\mathcal Y\), rational quantile grid \(\mathcal T\), and assertion list \(\mathscr A_{\mathrm{JC}}\) are fixed while \(n\to\infty\).
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument \(Z\), received treatment \(D\), and selection indicator \(S\) are binary; wages are observed only when \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Carter's experiment comparison is used only on fixed positive-support multinomial strata with \(\min_j(p_0)_j\ge\kappa\). The causal bridge separately maintains randomized-instrument and stratum positivity plus aggregate \(M_{\mathrm{ASC}}\ge m_{*}>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The local sequence now distinguishes three requirements. Base convergence \(p_n(0)\to p_0\) and the compact-uniform centered expansion imply \(\max_j\sup_{u\in C}|e_{n,j}(u)|\to0\) and \([B'\operatorname{diag}\{p_n(0)\}^{-1}B]^{-1}\to\Sigma_0\) on every rational compact \(C\). The zero-offset minimax target additionally requires \(c_n\to0\); a nonzero finite limit instead selects \(\mathfrak G_0(c)\). A computable moving schedule uses the separately declared effective remainder modulus. These compact statements do not by themselves control means escaping to infinity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.4 proves that recession cones form a rational fan under connectedness and the Minkowski--Weyl condition.
Theorems 3.32 and 4.8 construct a compatible compactified polyhedral complex and compute its Hasse diagram combinatorially.
Corollary 4 gives an explicit smoothing, truncation, and discretization error for Gaussian integration over a polytope.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a near-optimal affine detector for two compact convex composite hypotheses through a convex-concave saddle point.
Theorems 1--3 prove convergence of finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations to compact-parameter minimax expected-size confidence regions.
Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized \(O^*(n^3)\) relative-error algorithm for Gaussian volume of a convex set containing the unit ball in the membership-oracle model.
The paper gives convergence conditions for adaptive discretization of finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs with unbounded variables.
Theorem 1 bounds the Le Cam distance between a multinomial experiment and a matching Gaussian experiment when cell-probability ratios are bounded.
Theorem 3.1 establishes uniform coverage for calibrated projection under drifting moment inequalities, and Theorem 3.2 gives an optimization convergence rate on a compact rectangle.
The paper derives sharp marginal quantile-treatment-effect bounds under truncation by death.
Propositions 1--2 derive nonparametric bounds for average wage effects among always-employed compliers in Job Corps.

Under the complier-conditional weak-selection condition in Assumption 3.2, Proposition 3.1 gives sharp mean SLATE bounds for always-selected compliers, and Theorem 4.1 gives inference and joint asymptotic normality.

Theorem 1 proves minimum average Lebesgue volume for the inverted minimal-cardinality multinomial covering collections of Definition 1, and Proposition 1 selects a maximum-coverage tie-break among those minimizers.

Section 5 and Proposition 1 present sharp quantile-treatment-effect bounds for the always-employed stratum under random assignment and individual-level employment monotonicity, and Section 6.4 evaluates those bounds at multiple Job Corps wage quantiles.

body.tldr: The exact Gaussian decision value is now proved to attain its globally honest primal optimum and to equal the supremum of finite atomic dual certificates, with rational weights and real-algebraic supports dense without any spatial-support bound. The central effective incidence-density theorem, complete CertGluePFL stopping recurrence, and global Gaussian-to-multinomial transfer remain open. The corrected zero-offset transfer target explicitly requires \(c_n\to0\), compact-uniform moving-remainder convergence, and efficient-covariance convergence, while retaining both \(\liminf M_n\ge M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) and \(\limsup M_n\le M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\) as the required conclusion.

project_justification.gap: Existing compact decision theory and multinomial--Gaussian comparison do not provide the missing simultaneous rule approximation over an unbounded recession-incidence diagram or a single globally honest expanding-domain transfer. In particular, compact-local convergence of moving slacks does not control separated means escaping every fixed compact.
project_justification.niche: Finite-label partial-identification assertions create discontinuous loss and coverage constraints at intersecting faces, while least-favorable means and dual mass can escape along several incident cones. This structure is neither a compact convex hypothesis test nor a routine finite-dimensional semi-infinite program.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution currently supplies primal attainment, exact finite-atomic duality, dense rational/algebraic certificate enumeration, Gaussian smoothing, single-chart averaging, weighted path accounting, and exact full-set repair. The remaining program is to construct the effective compatible recession library and then propagate its ledger through a global transferred primal; the zero-offset, remainder, and covariance conditions for that transfer are now explicit.

body.related_work: Carter (2002, Theorem 1 and Sections 2--6) provides parameter-independent recursive multinomial--Gaussian comparison under positive cells, but the present proof spine still needs its quantitative bound transcribed and adapted to the declared score map, model-specific expansion error, moving faces, and semantic-union loss. Compact Gaussian decision results do not address globally honest rules on an unbounded fan, while drifting-moment-inequality results do not construct the required finite-label minimax transfer. The proved atomic duality here removes any bounded-support premise on least-favorable dual mass; the unresolved novelty is the effective incidence-compatible primal approximation and its global sampled-data transport.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Effective simultaneous incidence density, complete CertGluePFL recurrences, and the milliscale four-label certificate remain open. For sampled-data transfer, \(c_n\to0\), compact-uniform moving-remainder convergence, and covariance convergence identify the zero-offset experiment only on fixed compacts. No proof yet controls the rule and labels on separated means escaping every compact, so the reverse minimax inequality and hence two-sided convergence remain open. The causal fan also needs a compatible observed-law neighborhood, not merely multinomial cell interiority or compatibility at one base point.
body.honest_scope: Primal attainment and dense finite-atomic duality are unconditional for every encoded experiment in \(\mathfrak E\). Effective density and termination are not claimed proved. The compact-exhaustion theorem retains its two-sided minimax-convergence goal, now under explicit zero-offset, local-remainder, covariance, and compatible-base conditions; the globally honest expanding-domain primal is recorded as the unresolved step rather than replaced by a lower-only result. The causal identified set remains the same-law joint set and is only contained in the product of coordinatewise sharp intervals.
